groups.title: Terminology and classification
groups.blurb: Bass motion decides the cadence family; the treatment of ⑤ decides the form (simple / compound / double).

groups.title: Clausulae
groups.blurb: The melodic (polyphonic) view of the cadence: each voice has its own formula.

groups.title: Two-part cadences
groups.blurb: Discant (③–①… / ⑦–①) and tenor (②–①) cadences in simple, compound and double form.

groups.title: Three-part cadences
groups.blurb: Tenor-type (bass ②–①) and leaping (bass ⑤–①) cadences, plus Galant, Neapolitan, deceptive and Phrygian.

groups.title: Four-part cadences
groups.blurb: Every three-part cadence has a four-part equivalent; the fourth voice completes the chords and raises doubling questions.

patterns.name: Fenaroli’s three cadences
patterns.summary: A cadence is the bass going ①→⑤→①. Simple: plain consonances (3 and 5 over ①; major 3 and 5 over ⑤). Compound: a 4th over ⑤, prepared by the octave of ①, resolving to the major 3rd. Double: over ⑤ in turn 5/3, 6/4, 5/4, 5/3.
rules: Compound: the 4 over ⑤ must be prepared by the 8 of ① and resolve to the major 3.
Double: ⑤ lasts twice as long as in the compound cadence (four sonorities).
guidelines: Right-hand positions: 1st position (8 on top) closes most strongly; 2nd (3 on top) and 3rd (5 on top) are less conclusive.

checks: Fenaroli III (Gjerdingen ed.): definitions quoted in substance.
Demeyere: simple ⑤ = 1 beat, compound 2 beats (4–3, first sonority 5/4 or 6/4), double 4 beats.

patterns.name: Naming a cadence

sub.name: Perfect
sub.def: soprano and bass both on ①

sub.name: Phrygian half
sub.def: ⑥→⑤ half step in the bass (minor)

bassMotion.name: Evaded / Deceptive
bassMotion.bass: ⑤→ not ① (usually ⑥); also ⑤→④♯ (deceptive Neapolitan)

form.name: Double
form.def: simple + compound on a sustained ⑤ (5/3 – 6/4 – 5/4 – 5/3)

nomenclature.grammar: [Evaded | Deceptive]? + [Perfect | Imperfect] + [Simple | Compound | Double] + [Galant | Neapolitan | Discant | Alto | Tenor]? + [Half | Phrygian Half]? + Cadence

patterns.name: Clausula cantizans
patterns.summary: Clausula cantizans: (①–)⑦–①. When it lies in the bass the result is the discant cadence.
rules: Any of the four clausulae can be the bass; the others then appear in the remaining voices (invertible counterpoint).

rules: Any of the four clausulae can be the bass; the others then appear in the remaining voices (invertible counterpoint).

patterns.name: Jommelli cadence / extended SMP half cadence

patterns.name: Cadenza finta (feigned cadence)
patterns.summary: Valente’s term for Indugio variants that pretend to cadence: double pedal on ① and ③, or the interrupted circular Indugio (which may also be set as a deceptive cadence / deceptive Pulcinella).
